title: One Bad Cleaner Can Cost You Your Superhost Status — Here's How San Antonio Hosts Avoid It
meta_description: San Antonio Airbnb hosts: the questions to ask before hiring a turnover cleaning company — because one missed detail is all it takes to lose your rating.
content_html:
To avoid losing Superhost status over a bad cleaner, vet any cleaning company on six specifics before you hire them: what happens when something's missed, whether they require contracts, their same-day turnaround process, whether they're insured and vet their cleaners, whether you get photo proof of every turnover, and how they report damage. A company that answers with specifics instead of reassurance is the one worth hiring.

If you manage a short-term rental in San Antonio, you already know how fragile Superhost status is. It took dozens of clean stays to earn it — and it can slip in a single review. The biggest threat to that status usually isn't your decor or your check-in process. It's a cleaner who didn't show up, or showed up and missed something a guest noticed first.

Ask any group of Airbnb hosts what their top operational headache is, and "finding a cleaner I can actually rely on" comes up more than pricing, more than problem guests, more than platform fee changes. It's the thing that keeps hosts checking their phone an hour before check-in.

So before you hand someone the keys to your income property, here's what to actually ask — and what the answers tell you.

1. "What happens if a cleaner misses something?"

This is the single most revealing question you can ask a cleaning company. A company with weak systems will give you a vague answer — "we'll make it right" — with no explanation of how they'd even know something was missed before your guest does.

A company with real quality control will tell you about their process: photo documentation at checkout, a room-by-room checklist, a review step before the job is marked complete. If they can't describe a system, they don't have one — they have good intentions, which don't scale past the first bad week.

2. "Do you require contracts?"

This one surprises people, but it's worth asking directly. A lot of cleaning companies lock owners into 6- or 12-month contracts. On the surface that sounds like commitment. In practice, it's often the opposite — a contract is there so the company doesn't have to earn your business every single turnover, because you're stuck either way.

We don't use contracts at Chabod, and we're upfront about why: our checklists and quality-control process are the thing that keeps you with us, not a cancellation clause. If we start missing details, you should be free to leave. That's the deal. (More on that philosophy here: why we don't use contracts.)

3. "What's your turnaround process for same-day flips?"

Same-day turnovers — guest checks out at 11am, next guest checks in at 3pm — are where cleaning companies fall apart. Ask specifically: how do they get real-time notice that a guest has checked out? Is a cleaner already staged nearby, or are they starting from scratch once notified? What happens if the outgoing guest is late to leave?

Vague answers here predict missed turnovers later. You want specifics.

4. "Are you insured, and are your cleaners vetted?"

You're granting access to a property full of guest belongings and, often, your own furnishings. Ask directly about insurance coverage and how cleaners are screened before being assigned to your property. A company that hesitates on this question is telling you something.

5. "How do I know a job was actually done — not just marked done?"

This is where photo-based reporting matters. Ask whether you'll receive documentation after each turnover — not just a text saying "all done," but photo evidence tied to a checklist. If a guest later disputes cleanliness, you want a paper trail, not a he-said-she-said.

6. "What happens when something breaks or is damaged?"

Ask how damage gets reported. Same day? Photos included? Or do you find out three guests later when someone finally mentions the broken lamp? A cleaning company that documents damage proactively is protecting your reviews and your security deposit claims.

What good answers actually sound like

You're not looking for the cheapest quote — you're looking for the company that answers these questions with specifics instead of reassurance. "We photograph every room before we leave" is a specific answer. "We're very thorough" is not.

If a company can answer all six of these clearly, without hedging, that's a strong signal. If they can only answer the pricing question with confidence, that tells you where their actual attention goes.
